headline: On real violations (8 of 10 fixtures) v1 and v2 tied 16/16 — v1's general dependency-rule reasoning already generalizes well to novel violation shapes it was never given explicit rules for. The entire gap came from the 2 'clean/trap' fixtures: v1 twice misapplied the adapter-instantiation rule to a repository (a pattern both SKILL.mds explicitly sanction in their own canonical recipe), tipping its verdict to non-compliant. v2's added guidance ('an interface is not DI until something outside the module can substitute it' / clarifying repository-vs-adapter) fixed exactly that miscalibration without any regression on the violation fixtures.
caveat: n=1 run per cell on the Haiku model — directional, not a statistically robust benchmark. A rerun (or --model sonnet) could shift a close call like fake-port-not-wired's assertion B.
